import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Data preparation
# Filter out 'Mischling' (mixed breed) and 'Unbekannt' (unknown) from Rasse1Text
# as they often dominate and obscure specific breed insights.
breeds_to_exclude = ['Mischling', 'Unbekannt']
df_filtered_breeds = df[~df['Rasse1Text'].isin(breeds_to_exclude)].copy()

# Get the top N breeds by overall count
N_TOP_BREEDS = 10
top_breeds = df_filtered_breeds['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().nlargest(N_TOP_BREEDS).index

# Filter the DataFrame to include only these top breeds
df_top_breeds = df_filtered_breeds[df_filtered_breeds['Rasse1Text'].isin(top_breeds)].copy()

# Set plot style
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

# Create a countplot to visualize the distribution of top breeds by dog gender
# Using 'y' for Rasse1Text makes the breed names more readable.
sns.countplot(
    data=df_top_breeds,
    y='Rasse1Text',
    hue='SexHundLang',
    order=top_breeds, # Ensure breeds are ordered from most to least common
    palette='viridis'
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title(f'Top {N_TOP_BREEDS} Dog Breeds in Zurich by Gender (Excluding Mixed/Unknown Breeds)', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Number of Dogs', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Breed', fontsize=12)
plt.legend(title='Dog Gender', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Improve layout and save the figure
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
